fcdo.title: UK Government foreign travel advice (Open Government Licence v3.0)

entry.en: Your passport must be valid for the length of your stay in Japan, with no additional validity period required.
entry.es: El pasaporte debe ser válido durante su estancia en Japón, sin exigirse un periodo adicional de validez.
entry.quote: your passport must be valid for the length of your stay. No additional period of validity is required.

entry.en: It is illegal to bring meat products such as sausages, bacon and ham into Japan without permission from the Japanese Animal Quarantine Service.
entry.es: Es ilegal llevar a Japón productos cárnicos como salchichas, beicon y jamón sin permiso del Servicio de Cuarentena Animal japonés.
entry.quote: It is illegal to bring meat products including sausages, bacon and ham to Japan without permission from the Japanese Animal Quarantine Service.

entry.en: Foreigners must typically fill out a disembarkation form for immigration and a declaration form for customs, and the Visit Japan Web service can be used to submit them in advance.
entry.es: Los extranjeros suelen tener que rellenar un formulario de desembarco y una declaración de aduanas, que pueden enviarse antes con el servicio Visit Japan Web.
entry.quote: The Visit Japan Web service can be used to electronically submit all required forms in advance.

entry.en: Some common medicines, including those with pseudoephedrine, are illegal to carry under Japan's anti-stimulant drugs law.
entry.es: Llevar algunos medicamentos comunes, incluidos los que contienen pseudoefedrina, es ilegal según la ley japonesa sobre estimulantes.
entry.quote: It is illegal to carry some common prescription and over-the-counter medicines under Japan’s strictly enforced law on anti-stimulant drugs.

safety.en: In Tokyo's entertainment districts, foreign nationals have been targeted for extortion, robbery, assault and sexual assault, particularly at night around clubs and bars.
safety.es: En los barrios de ocio de Tokio, se ha atacado a extranjeros con extorsión, robo y agresiones, sobre todo de noche cerca de clubes y bares.
safety.quote: Tokyo’s entertainment districts carry a higher risk of crime, particularly at night in and around clubs and bars. Foreign nationals have been targeted for extortion, robbery, assault and sexual assault.

safety.en: There are increased reports of drink spiking and credit card fraud, and victims are advised not to follow street touts into bars.
safety.es: Hay más denuncias de drogado de bebidas y fraude con tarjetas, y se aconseja no seguir a los captadores callejeros a los bares.
safety.quote: There are increased reports of drink spiking and credit card fraud.

safety.en: Japan is in a major earthquake zone.
safety.es: Japón se encuentra en una importante zona sísmica.
safety.quote: Japan is in a major earthquake zone.

safety.en: The typhoon season runs from June to December, peaking between July and September, with the highest risk in southern parts of the country.
safety.es: La temporada de tifones va de junio a diciembre, con el máximo entre julio y septiembre y el mayor riesgo en el sur.
safety.quote: the tropical cyclone (typhoon) season is between June and December, peaking between July and September. The highest risk is in southern parts of the country.

safety.en: There is zero tolerance of drug crime in Japan and the penalties are severe.
safety.es: En Japón hay tolerancia cero con los delitos de drogas y las penas son severas.
safety.quote: There is zero tolerance of drug crime and the penalties are severe.

safety.en: Bear sightings and attacks have increased in parts of Japan, especially in mountainous and forested areas.
safety.es: Han aumentado los avistamientos y ataques de osos en partes de Japón, sobre todo en zonas montañosas y boscosas.
safety.quote: Bear sightings and attacks have increased in parts of Japan, especially in mountainous and forested areas

health.en: Medical facilities in Japan are of a high quality, but treatment is expensive and you are expected to pay the whole cost.
health.es: Los centros médicos de Japón son de alta calidad, pero el tratamiento es caro y hay que pagar el coste completo.
health.quote: Medical facilities in Japan are of a high quality, but treatment is expensive. Expect to pay the whole cost of any treatment you receive.

health.en: Tap water is safe and of good quality throughout Japan.
health.es: El agua del grifo es segura y de buena calidad en todo Japón.
health.quote: Tap water is safe and of good quality throughout the country.

health.en: Japan has no communicable diseases of significance and food hygiene standards are very high.
health.es: En Japón no hay enfermedades transmisibles de importancia y los estándares de higiene alimentaria son muy altos.
health.quote: Food hygiene standards are very high and there are no communicable diseases of significance.

health.en: Heat stroke and heat-related illnesses pose a significant risk during the summer months.
health.es: El golpe de calor y otras enfermedades por calor suponen un riesgo importante en verano.
health.quote: heat stroke and heat-related illnesses pose a significant risk during the summer months.

health.en: The 24/7 Japan Visitor Hotline for emergency English-language assistance during natural disasters is +81(5)0 3816 2787.
health.es: La línea de ayuda para visitantes de Japón, 24 horas, ofrece asistencia de emergencia en inglés en desastres naturales: +81(5)0 3816 2787.
health.quote: The Japan National Tourism Organisation operates a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week Japan Visitor Hotline for emergency English-language assistance during natural disasters

health.en: Short-term tourists cannot use the national health insurance system, so travel insurance should be arranged before the trip.
health.es: Los turistas de corta estancia no pueden usar el seguro de salud nacional, así que conviene contratar un seguro de viaje antes.
health.quote: it is not available to tourists on short visits, so be sure to have your travel insurance in order before your trip.

help.en: The emergency numbers in Japan are 119 for ambulance and fire and 110 for police.
help.es: Los números de emergencia en Japón son el 119 para ambulancia y bomberos y el 110 para la policía.

help.en: FCDO can be called in London on 020 7008 5000, 24 hours, if something has happened to a friend or relative abroad.
help.es: Se puede llamar al FCDO en Londres al 020 7008 5000, las 24 horas, si ha ocurrido algo a un amigo o familiar en el extranjero.
help.quote: You can call FCDO in London if you need urgent help because something has happened to a friend or relative abroad.

getting_in.en: Most international flights arrive at Narita or Haneda airports near Tokyo, or Kansai Airport near Osaka.
getting_in.es: La mayoría de los vuelos internacionales llegan a los aeropuertos de Narita o Haneda, cerca de Tokio, o al de Kansai, cerca de Osaka.
getting_in.quote: Most international flights arrive at Narita Airport (NRT IATA) or Haneda Airport (HND IATA) near Tokyo, or Kansai Airport (KIX IATA) near Osaka.

getting_in.en: Many flights from major Asian cities also serve Chubu Centrair near Nagoya, Fukuoka Airport and Chitose Airport near Sapporo.
getting_in.es: Muchos vuelos desde grandes ciudades asiáticas también llegan a Chubu Centrair (Nagoya), Fukuoka y Chitose (Sapporo).
getting_in.quote: Many flights from major Asian cities also serve Chubu Centrair Airport (NGO IATA) near Nagoya, Fukuoka Airport (FUK IATA) on Kyushu Island, and Chitose Airport (CTS IATA) near Sapporo, Hokkaido Island.

getting_in.en: There are international ferries to Japan from South Korea, China and Taiwan.
getting_in.es: Hay ferris internacionales a Japón desde Corea del Sur, China y Taiwán.
getting_in.quote: There are international ferries to Japan from South Korea, China and Taiwan.

getting_around.en: Trains are the most popular way of getting around Japan and are generally very punctual except during bad weather or natural disasters.
getting_around.es: El tren es la opción más popular en Japón y suele ser muy puntual, salvo con mal tiempo o desastres naturales.
getting_around.quote: Trains are generally very punctual except during inclement weather or natural disasters.

getting_around.en: Transport IC cards can pay for public transport and at convenience stores, vending machines and restaurants in all the major cities.
getting_around.es: Las tarjetas IC de transporte sirven para el transporte público y para pagar en tiendas de conveniencia, máquinas expendedoras y restaurantes de las grandes ciudades.
getting_around.quote: IC cards can be used to pay for public transport and at convenience stores, vending machines and restaurants in all the major cities.

getting_around.en: The Japan Rail Pass offers, with a few exceptions, unlimited travel on all JR services, but you need to travel a lot for it to pay off now.
getting_around.es: El Japan Rail Pass permite, con pocas excepciones, viajar sin límite en los servicios JR, pero hoy hay que viajar mucho para que compense.
getting_around.quote: The Japan Rail Pass offers — with a few exceptions — unlimited travel on all Japan Railway (JR) services including bullet trains, limited express and regular commuter trains.

getting_around.en: Most roads in Japan have no name, so maps and navigation apps are a great help.
getting_around.es: La mayoría de las calles de Japón no tienen nombre, así que los mapas y las aplicaciones de navegación son de gran ayuda.
getting_around.quote: The lack of road names makes it difficult to give directions; maps and especially navigation apps are a blessing in Japan.

getting_around.en: Drivers in Japan need the 1949 version of the international driving permit plus their UK licence, and driving is on the left.
getting_around.es: En Japón se necesita la versión de 1949 del permiso internacional de conducir junto con el carné británico, y se conduce por la izquierda.
getting_around.quote: You’ll need the 1949 version of the international driving permit (IDP) plus your UK driving licence and insurance documents with you in the car.

getting_around.en: Flying is the most practical way to reach Japan's outlying islands, notably Hokkaido and Okinawa.
getting_around.es: Volar es la forma más práctica de llegar a las islas periféricas de Japón, sobre todo Hokkaido y Okinawa.
getting_around.quote: Flying remains, however, the most practical mode of reaching Japan's outlying islands, most notably for connections from the mainland to Hokkaido and/or Okinawa.

money.en: The Japanese currency is the yen, abbreviated ¥ or JPY.
money.es: La moneda japonesa es el yen, abreviado ¥ o JPY.
money.quote: The Japanese currency is the Japanese yen, abbreviated ¥ (or JPY in foreign exchange contexts).

money.en: Japan is still a predominantly cash-based society and cards issued outside Japan may be difficult to use.
money.es: Japón sigue siendo una sociedad basada sobre todo en el efectivo y puede costar usar tarjetas emitidas fuera del país.
money.quote: Japan is still a predominantly cash-based society. You may have difficulty using credit and debit cards issued outside Japan.

money.en: ATMs are ubiquitous in Japan, and 7-Eleven Bank ATMs are usually open 24/7.
money.es: Los cajeros son omnipresentes en Japón y los de 7-Eleven Bank suelen estar abiertos las 24 horas.
money.quote: A particularly convenient option for travelers is 7-Eleven Bank ATMs, which can be found in every branch of 7-Eleven and are usually open 24/7.

money.en: Most ATMs charge ¥110 or ¥220 for withdrawals.
money.es: La mayoría de los cajeros cobran 110 o 220 yenes por retirada.
money.quote: Most ATMs charge ¥110 or ¥220 for withdrawals

money.en: Quite a few restaurants, small shops and even some lodgings only accept cash, particularly in smaller towns and more isolated areas.
money.es: Bastantes restaurantes, tiendas pequeñas e incluso algunos alojamientos solo aceptan efectivo, sobre todo en pueblos pequeños y zonas aisladas.
money.quote: Quite a few restaurants, small shops, and even some lodgings only accept cash, particularly in smaller towns and more isolated areas.

money.en: Visa, MasterCard and JCB credit and debit cards are widely accepted.
money.es: Las tarjetas de crédito y débito Visa, MasterCard y JCB son ampliamente aceptadas.
money.quote: Credit and debit cards are widely accepted, but some cafes, bars, and restaurants may still only accept cash and/or IC card. Visa, MasterCard and JCB are widely accepted.

etiquette.en: The text says never to walk on a tatami mat wearing shoes or even slippers.
etiquette.es: El texto indica que nunca se debe pisar un tatami con zapatos ni siquiera con zapatillas.
etiquette.quote: Never walk on a tatami mat wearing shoes or even slippers, as it would damage the tatami.

etiquette.en: The text says never to leave chopsticks standing upright in a bowl of rice.
etiquette.es: El texto indica que nunca se deben dejar los palillos clavados en vertical en un cuenco de arroz.
etiquette.quote: Never leave your chopsticks standing upright in a bowl of rice (this is how rice is offered to the dead).

etiquette.en: The text says never to enter a bathtub without washing yourself thoroughly first.
etiquette.es: El texto indica que nunca se debe entrar en una bañera sin lavarse a fondo antes.
etiquette.quote: Never enter a bathtub without washing yourself thoroughly first.

etiquette.en: Loud, boisterous behaviour may receive negative attention in Japan.
etiquette.es: El comportamiento ruidoso y escandaloso puede recibir atención negativa en Japón.
etiquette.quote: Loud, boisterous behaviour may receive negative attention.

etiquette.en: Some public facilities, such as swimming pools, hot springs, beaches and some gyms, do not admit people with tattoos.
etiquette.es: Algunas instalaciones públicas, como piscinas, aguas termales, playas y algunos gimnasios, no admiten a personas con tatuajes.
etiquette.quote: some public facilities do not admit people with tattoos – for example, public swimming pools, hot springs, beaches and some gyms.

etiquette.en: When handing something over, especially a business card, it is considered polite to present it with both hands.
etiquette.es: Al entregar algo, sobre todo una tarjeta de visita, se considera educado hacerlo con ambas manos.
etiquette.quote: When you are handing something to someone, especially a business card, it is considered polite to present it holding it with both hands.

connectivity.en: Roaming through your home carrier is almost certainly the easiest option, and 3G/2G phones do not work in Japan.
connectivity.es: El roaming con la operadora propia es casi seguro lo más fácil, y los móviles 3G/2G no funcionan en Japón.
connectivity.quote: Purchasing a roaming plan from your carrier is almost certainly the easiest option to maintain mobile service in Japan.

connectivity.en: eSIMs are widely available, and the easiest place to buy a prepaid tourist SIM is the airport after passing through customs.
connectivity.es: Las eSIM están muy disponibles y el lugar más fácil para comprar una SIM turística de prepago es el aeropuerto tras pasar la aduana.
connectivity.quote: By far the easiest place to do this is at the airport after passing through customs. eSIMs are widely available

connectivity.en: Bic Camera or Yodobashi Camera stores sell prepaid SIMs if you cannot buy one at the airport.
connectivity.es: Las tiendas Bic Camera o Yodobashi Camera venden SIM de prepago si no se puede comprar una en el aeropuerto.
connectivity.quote: If you can't purchase a SIM at the airport, your best options in town are usually a Bic Camera or Yodobashi Camera store.
